first_impression.reaction: My assistant flagged this one, and the opening is calm and doesn't try to sell me anything. 'It starts weeks or months earlier, in a living room' is how it really happens in our family. I kept going, but as a culture piece, not as evidence that this team can run my wedding.

journey.quote: A Lebanese wedding rarely starts on the wedding day. It starts weeks or months earlier, in a living room, when one family visits another to ask a question.
journey.reaction: Understated, accurate, no gushing. A good first screen.

journey.quote: So customs vary between Christian, Muslim and Druze families, and between regions and households within each.
journey.reaction: They don't flatten us into one stereotype. That matters to me more than any photo.

journey.quote: In Arab weddings generally, the families reading the Fatiha after the father agrees is described as typically accompanied by Arabic coffee in the Levant, though that account is framed around Muslim families in Egypt, Palestine and Jordan rather than Lebanon.
journey.reaction: Too much hedging and sourcing. It reads like a footnote, not someone who has actually sat in these rooms. My assistant would skim past this.

journey.section: The church ceremony and the crowning
journey.quote: One line stands out for Lebanese couples: a crowning prayer in the Orthodox text asks God to "exalt them like the cedars of Lebanon, like a luxuriant vine".
journey.reaction: A lovely detail. This is the kind of thing that tells me someone paid attention.

journey.section: Bringing Lebanese customs to a wedding abroad
journey.quote: Couples bring these customs to lake villas in Italy, beach venues in Cyprus, ballrooms in the UAE and family-sized receptions in Australia.
journey.reaction: Lake Como is the right register. But nothing tells me they've done this for 300 guests with the whole villa closed off.

journey.section: Space for the zaffeh and the dabke line
journey.quote: A zaffeh needs a route, not just a doorway: a clear path from where the couple arrive to the dance floor, wide enough for drummers and dancers, with guests on either side.
journey.reaction: Practical and right. Someone has thought about logistics, which is what I'd actually be paying for.

journey.section: Timing a henna night around travel
journey.quote: A private dining room or a villa's lounge suits it better than a public space.
journey.reaction: Good instinct on privacy, but it stops there. For us the question is whether the whole property is closed, not which room.

journey.section: Blades, venue rules and the cake
journey.quote: Your Advisor is a single point of contact who plans the venue, travel and vendors, agrees the fee in writing before any work begins, and confirms what is included in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Clear and unfussy. Still sounds built for a normal couple; no mention of working alongside a family office, our own security, or VIP guests.

journey.quote: When you are ready to talk dates and places, a Wedded Advisor is glad to start the conversation.
journey.reaction: Polite enough. 'Glad to' is a touch eager, but not off-putting.

unanswered_questions: Have they delivered Lebanese weddings of 200 to 400 guests, and can they show that privately?
Can they arrange exclusive use of a villa or property across a multi-day programme (henna, katb al-kitab or crowning, reception)?
How do they handle discretion: NDAs for vendors, no social posting, guest phone policy?
Will they coordinate with our own security team and arrange private transfers for VIP guests?
Can they bring in Lebanese caterers, sweets makers and zaffeh troupes abroad, or only use the venue's suppliers?
Is there a private or referral route to an Advisor rather than a general web form?

turn_offs_found.quote: or [read the free Wedded Wonderland digital magazine]
turn_offs_found.why: 'Free' is mass-market language. Mild, but it signals they are speaking to a different client from me.

would_share_with: My mother, for the crowning prayer line and the henna night section
My assistant, as background for briefing planners

cta_reaction.quote: If you would like one person to hold all of this together, you can [speak with a Wedded Advisor]
cta_reaction.why: I like the single point of contact and the tone isn't pushy. But I only enquire through a private channel or a referral, and nothing here shows they can handle our scale or keep it quiet. My assistant might note the name, nothing more yet.

top_3_changes: In the abroad section, add one understated line on large guest numbers and exclusive use (whole-villa or multi-day buyouts), so a family like mine sees this team plans at scale.
Mention discretion and security plainly: private transfers, working alongside a family's own security, and keeping the day off social media.
Trim the source hedging in the tulbeh and henna sections so it reads like lived knowledge, and drop 'free' from the magazine link.
